These watches offer extensive tracking features for runners and triathletes, with the 965 boasting advanced mapping and longer battery life. The prices are Rs 67,490 for the Forerunner 965 and Rs 50,490 for the 265 series, and they are available both online and offline.

title: Masimo v. Apple – Judge Declares a Mistrial as Jury Hopelessly Deadlocked
summary: A mistrial has been declared in the $1.8 billion trade secret lawsuit between Masimo Corp. and Apple Inc. after the jury became hopelessly deadlocked, leaning significantly towards Apple's defense. Both companies are expected to pursue a new trial, with Masimo planning to retry the case and Apple seeking to dismiss the remaining claims. The article suggests Masimo may have been overconfident due to previous wins against Apple, while Apple's legal team presented a strong defense.

title: Apple fights $2 billion London lawsuit for 'throttling' millions of iPhones
summary: Apple is facing a substantial $2 billion lawsuit in London, accused of "throttling" millions of iPhones by covertly installing software updates to manage defective batteries. Consumer advocate Justin Gutmann, representing UK iPhone users, claims Apple concealed battery issues and limited performance. Apple denies these allegations, calling the lawsuit "baseless" and stating that their power management update only minimally affected performance for certain older models, while offering free battery replacements for a small number of iPhone 6s models.

title: Qualcomm outlook grim as smartphone sales stay weak
summary: Qualcomm Inc. forecast third-quarter revenue and profit below Wall Street estimates due to weak smartphone sales and excess chip inventory. The company's CEO noted a lack of meaningful recovery, particularly in China, and faces increased competition and a rise in used phone sales impacting premium device demand. Qualcomm's shares fell nearly 7% after the announcement.

title: Joe Kiani, Co-founder and CEO of Masimo, Talks About Fighting Corporate Giants and His Fixation on Reducing Preventable Hospital Deaths
summary: Joe Kiani, co-founder and CEO of Masimo, discusses his journey from an immigrant to a medtech innovator. He recounts how he started Masimo to create a more reliable pulse oximeter after encountering disinterest from his previous employer. Kiani also touches on Masimo's legal battles with Apple, its acquisition of Sound United, and his ongoing advocacy for reducing preventable hospital deaths and addressing homelessness.

title: CEO Tim Cook says layoffs are a 'last resort' and not something Apple is considering right now
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook stated that large-scale layoffs are a "last resort" and not currently being considered by the company, contrasting with many other Big Tech firms that have cut thousands of jobs. While not ruling out future job cuts, Apple is focusing on cost-cutting measures and a slower rate of hiring. The company remains highly profitable, reporting $24 billion in net income on $95 billion in revenue for its March quarter.

title: Amkor Technology seeks to open Vietnam factory in fourth quarter
summary: U.S.-based Amkor Technology Inc. expects its mega facility in Bac Ninh, Vietnam, to begin first-phase manufacturing in the fourth quarter of this year. This factory, covering 1.9 million square feet, will be among Amkor's largest globally and represents a $1.6 billion investment until 2035. The move highlights Vietnam's growing importance as a manufacturing and R&D hub for major foreign electronics manufacturers.

title: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway has been a fortress stock during recessions and bear markets. Here's how
summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway has proven to be a resilient investment, consistently outperforming the S&P 500 during recessions and bear markets due to its long-term focus and conservative investment strategies. The conglomerate's significant stake in Apple, coupled with its substantial cash reserves and insurance ventures, underscores its "fortress stock" reputation. This approach has led to impressive compounded annual gains for Berkshire shareholders over decades.

title: Apple stakes future growth on emerging markets, starting with India
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook is betting on emerging markets, particularly India, for future growth after iPhone sales surprisingly rose despite a global smartphone slump. The company sees significant opportunity in these markets due to their youthful populations and low iPhone penetration, with India showing strong double-digit growth and becoming a major focus for Apple. The booming used iPhone market also contributes to Apple's market share gains in these regions.

title: Buffett says Apple is Berkshire portfolio's best business
summary: Warren Buffett stated that Apple Inc. is a better business than any other in Berkshire Hathaway Inc.'s portfolio, citing its dominant consumer product, the iPhone. Berkshire Hathaway's stake in Apple grew from $1 billion in 2016 to $151 billion by March 2023, accounting for 46% of its equity portfolio, and Buffett indicated the company could buy more shares. He views Apple primarily as a consumer products company rather than a technology company.

title: My Favorite BlackBerry of All Time Is One That Everyone Hated
summary: The author reminisces about the BlackBerry PlayBook, a 7-inch tablet launched in 2011, which he believes was ahead of its time despite being largely panned by critics. He highlights its innovative hardware design, multitasking-focused QNX software, and gestures that foreshadowed features in modern tablets. The article concludes that while the PlayBook was ultimately doomed by poor strategic decisions like the lack of core apps and third-party developer support, many of its ideas live on in today's successful tablets.

title: CEO pay continues to soar – new study
summary: A new study by Equilar reveals that median CEO pay at top US public companies increased by 7.7% to a record $22.3 million in 2022, despite negative S&P 500 returns. This rise was primarily driven by stock awards, leading to a median "pay ratio" of 288 times the median employee's compensation, significantly outpacing the 3.6% increase in average US private sector employee earnings. The study highlights a trend of incentivizing executives through substantial stock awards during uncertain economic times.

summary: The article analyzes Yeti Holdings (NYSE: YETI), highlighting its impressive gross profit margins, which surpass those of Apple and Nike. The author examines Yeti's pricing power and quality products but expresses concerns about the unpredictable nature of future sales and potential growth limitations due to the durability of its products. Ultimately, the author concludes that Yeti's long-term outlook isn't inspiring enough to warrant an investment at this time.

title: IonQ Appoints Pat Tang as VP of Research & Development
summary: IonQ, a quantum computing leader, announced the appointment of Pat Tang as Vice President of Research and Development. Tang, previously an Engineering Vice President at Amazon Lab126 and a team lead at Apple, will lead the company's technical exploration with a focus on developing impactful technologies for IonQ's systems. His extensive experience in building and scaling innovative technologies is expected to be invaluable as IonQ continues to advance quantum computing.

title: Layoffs may cause organizational drag: Gartner
summary: According to Gartner research, layoffs can negatively impact shareholder returns within three years by leading to reduced employee morale, increased turnover, and loss of customers, despite initial cost savings. The report highlights that businesses often face immediate costs like severance payments and long-term issues such as higher contractor costs and demands for increased compensation from remaining staff. Gartner suggests alternative cost-cutting measures like voluntary reduced hours, executive pay cuts, hiring freezes, and internal redeployment to avoid "organizational drag."

title: Apple previews Live Speech, Personal Voice, and more new accessibility features
summary: Apple announced new accessibility features including Assistive Access for cognitive disabilities, Live Speech and Personal Voice for speech accessibility, and Point and Speak in Magnifier for users who are blind or have low vision. These features leverage advances in hardware and software, including on-device machine learning for privacy, and are part of Apple's ongoing commitment to making technology inclusive for everyone. The company also detailed various initiatives and events celebrating Global Accessibility Awareness Day, showcasing applications of these features and broader accessibility efforts across its products and services.

title: Apple investments with European suppliers surpass €20 billion annual spend
summary: Apple announced that its investments with European suppliers exceeded €20 billion in 2022, reaching a total of €85 billion over the last five years. These investments support over 4,000 European suppliers, fostering innovation in Apple products and advancing the green transition of European industry, while also supporting more than 2.6 million jobs across the region. The company is committed to achieving carbon neutrality across its supply chain by 2030, with many European partners joining its Supplier Clean Energy Program.

summary: Online shopping app Temu, owned by Chinese company PDD Holdings Inc., has quickly risen to popularity in Canada with its aggressive marketing, low prices, and gamified shopping experience. The platform's "growth-at-all-costs" approach and referral schemes are disrupting the e-commerce market, leading to a "race to the bottom" that could hurt local businesses.

summary: The article compares Cadence (CDNS) and Synopsys (SNPS), two leading electronic design automation (EDA) software providers, to determine which stock is a better investment. The authors conclude that Synopsys has a slight edge due to its higher EDA market share, strong position in intellectual property, and marginally better valuation, despite both being considered overvalued.

title: Everything you need to know about Salesforce’s Q1 2024 financial results
summary: Salesforce, Inc. reported increased first-quarter adjusted earnings in Q1 2024 ($1.69 per share) and revenue growth of 11% year-over-year to $8.25 billion. All key operating segments showed growth, driven by its generative AI ecosystem including Einstein GPT, Slack GPT, and Tableau GPT. CEO Marc Benioff highlighted the role of the Salesforce GPT Trust Layer in securing customer data and enhancing enterprise automation.

title: American Express Is Approaching Generative AI Technology with Caution
summary: American Express is cautiously approaching generative AI technology, aiming to integrate it for enhanced personalization, proactivity, and predictive capabilities through partnerships rather than developing its own large language models. This cautious stance aligns with broader industry concerns, highlighted by an open letter from tech leaders urging a pause in "giant AI experiments" to establish safety protocols. Amex Digital Labs, established in 2017, serves as the company's innovation hub for product prototypes and predictive analytics.

title: Apple Dominates Berkshire’s Portfolio. The Tech Stock Is Near a Record.
summary: Apple stock is approaching a record high and has become the dominant holding in Berkshire Hathaway's investment portfolio. This article details the significance of Apple's performance for Warren Buffett's company.

title: Garmin debuts Pro versions of Fenix 7 and Epix 7 adventure smartwatches
summary: Garmin has launched Pro versions of its Fenix 7 and Epix 2 smartwatches, introducing new sizes and features. Both Pro models include a redesigned, more accurate heart-rate sensor, a built-in LED flashlight with variable intensities, and enhanced mapping features. The Fenix 7 Pro adds endurance and hill scores, while the Epix 2 Pro, which features an AMOLED display, gains additional activity options and a Red Shift mode.

title: Apple Bets On The Emerging Markets Growth Story
summary: Apple is increasingly focusing on emerging markets, particularly India, to drive growth amidst a challenging global smartphone market. The company achieved marginal growth in iPhone sales despite overall industry decline, with India seeing significant retail and manufacturing expansion plans. While services and financial technology offer long-term opportunities, the emerging markets strategy is a key component of Apple's immediate growth narrative, alongside ongoing share repurchases and dividend increases.

title: Apple, Microsoft Boost the S&P 500 Amid Tech Comeback
summary: Apple and Microsoft have significantly contributed to the S&P 500's gains in 2023, accounting for nearly half of the index's rise and reaching an all-time high combined weight of 14%. The article suggests leveraged ETFs like AAPU, MSFU, and TECL for traders looking to capitalize on the continued bullish trend in the tech sector.

summary: The Invesco S&P 500 High Beta ETF (SPHB) performed strongly in May, driven by its significant allocation to the information technology sector. SPHB has also demonstrated strong long-term performance, outpacing the S&P 500 over a three-year period.

title: PayPal and Venmo users shouldn't store money on the apps long term
summary: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) has warned users against storing money long-term on payment apps like PayPal, Venmo, and CashApp, citing potential risks during a financial crisis. Unlike traditional bank accounts, funds held in these apps are generally not covered by FDIC insurance, leaving them vulnerable if the platform experiences financial distress. While some specific features like PayPal Savings or Apple Cash with identity verification may offer insurance, the default accounts typically do not.

title: Vimeo is tuning out its streaming TV apps
summary: Vimeo is discontinuing its dedicated streaming TV apps for Apple TV, Android TV, Amazon Fire TV, and Roku starting June 27th. Users can still watch Vimeo content on their TVs by casting from the Vimeo mobile app via Apple AirPlay 2 or Google Chromecast. This move aligns with Vimeo's strategic shift in recent years from a consumer-facing streaming destination to focusing on video-streaming services for businesses.

title: In challenge to Meta, Apple expected to unveil mixed-reality headset
summary: Apple is expected to announce a new mixed-reality headset at its annual software developer conference, positioning itself against Meta Platforms in the emerging market for virtual and augmented reality. While Meta's CEO Mark Zuckerberg has championed the "metaverse" and has products out, Apple has been more private about its augmented-reality efforts, which so far have been limited to existing devices. Analysts suggest Apple's device, rumored to cost around $3,000, is an interim step toward transparent augmented-reality glasses and aims to encourage software developers to create compelling "XR" applications where no "killer app" currently exists.

title: Introducing Apple Vision Pro: Apple’s first spatial computer
summary: Apple has unveiled Apple Vision Pro, its first spatial computer, which blends digital content with the physical world using a three-dimensional user interface controlled by eyes, hands, and voice. Running on the new visionOS, Vision Pro features an ultra-high-resolution display system, custom Apple silicon, and offers new ways to interact with apps, enjoy entertainment, relive memories, and connect via FaceTime. The device is designed with advanced materials, focuses on privacy, and will be available early next year starting at $3,499 (U.S.).

title: Is Temu Shopping App a Communist China-Based Scam That Spies on Users?
summary: This article investigates claims that the Temu shopping app, owned by Chinese company PDD Holdings, is a scam that spies on users. It critically examines assertions made in a widely shared USA Today column, confirming that while concerns about product quality, data practices, and the company's Chinese ties are valid, some claims about the app's ability to access phone data without consent are imprecise or relate to its sister app, Pinduoduo, which was found to contain malware. The article concludes that Temu offers legitimate cheap products but its parent company's business ethics and data privacy record raise significant concerns.

summary: A federal judge in Seattle has ruled that Apple and Amazon must face a consumer antitrust lawsuit accusing them of conspiring to artificially inflate the price of iPhones and iPads sold on Amazon's platform. The lawsuit alleges that a 2019 agreement between the two companies restricted the number of competitive resellers, a claim that will now proceed to evidence-gathering. Apple contends the agreement was to minimize counterfeit goods and is procompetitive.

title: Labor Ruling Offers Unionization Path to Uber, Lyft Drivers
summary: A recent U.S. labor board ruling has made it easier for workers to be classified as employees rather than independent contractors, potentially opening the door for unionization efforts among gig workers at companies like Uber and Lyft. While gig companies argue this could impact their business model, the decision emboldens organizing campaigns, despite the inherent difficulties in unionizing a dispersed workforce. This ruling could lead to significant challenges for gig companies, potentially forcing them to negotiate with unions, though hurdles remain for successful organizing drives.

title: Sonos Era 300 Review: Spatial Audio Is a Game Changer
summary: The Sonos Era 300 is the company's first speaker designed specifically for spatial audio, aiming to revolutionize how we experience music beyond traditional stereo. While it boasts a unique design and offers good stereo performance with Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.0 connectivity, its key selling point is the immersive spatial audio experience, particularly with services like Amazon Music Unlimited and Apple Music. Although pricey at $449 and limited in spatial audio service support at launch, the Era 300 delivers impressive sound quality that justifies the investment, especially when considering its potential as rear surround speakers for a home theater setup.

title: Lenovo ‘overall winner’ of UK FRAND trial as InterDigital confirms appeal
summary: The UK High Court has declared Lenovo the 'overall winner' in its FRAND dispute with InterDigital, determining a FRAND rate of $138.7 million plus $46.2 million in interest, making the total $184.9 million. The court found Lenovo's proposed per-unit rate much closer to the final decision than InterDigital's, and the payable lump sum 'substantially lower' than InterDigital's offer. Both parties have been granted permission to appeal this decision, indicating the case is not yet concluded.

title: Apple, world's most valuable public company, is first to hit $3 trillion in market value

title: Apple’s market value ends above $3 trillion for the first time

title: Apple loses London appeal in 4G patent dispute with Optis
summary: London's Court of Appeal dismissed Apple's appeal in a patent dispute with Optis Cellular Technology LLC, ruling that Apple infringed two 4G telecommunications patents. Texas-based Optis sued Apple in 2019, alleging that the patents are essential to certain technological standards used in devices like iPhones and iPads. This ruling is the latest decision in a legal battle that has involved multiple trials and appeals in Britain.

title: Apple executives fight subpoenas in shareholders' lawsuit against Qualcomm
summary: Apple Inc.'s chief operating officer and a top corporate lawyer are attempting to quash subpoenas in a private securities class action lawsuit against chipmaker Qualcomm. Apple contends that Qualcomm is using the subpoenas to harass the company.

The expansion comes as Apple recorded a significant market share in China's smartphone market despite an overall decline in sales.

summary: Nasdaq announced a special rebalance of the Nasdaq-100 Index to dilute the weightings of mega-cap tech stocks that have outperformed in 2023. The seven largest stocks in the Nasdaq-100 will see their combined weighting reduced from 56% to 44%, with Nvidia and Microsoft being most affected. Historically, similar rebalances have not had a significant impact on stock prices.

title: Preparing for Upcoming QQQ Changes
summary: Nasdaq is implementing a special rebalance of its Nasdaq-100 Index (NDX), impacting ETFs like Invesco QQQ (QQQ) and Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF (QQQM). This rebalance, effective July 24, aims to address concentration risk due to the large percentage holdings of tech giants like Microsoft and Apple. Investors can expect lower allocations to these mega-cap growth names, though the overall changes are not anticipated to be monumental, and the ETF structure should help avoid capital gains distributions for investors.

title: Apple maintains its spot as the world’s most valuable brand, per Kantar BrandZ
summary: Apple has retained its position as the world's most valuable brand according to Kantar BrandZ, valued at $880,455M, despite a 7% decline from 2022. The company's resilience is attributed to its strong brand equity, diversification into services, and ability to justify premium pricing. Apple's differentiation, purpose-driven initiatives, distinctive products, and iconic advertising are highlighted as key factors in its sustained success amidst challenging market conditions.

title: Report: Apple built ‘Apple GPT’ chatbot using internal AI development framework
summary: Apple Inc. has reportedly developed an internal AI framework called Ajax for building large language models and a ChatGPT-like chatbot internally known as "Apple GPT." Ajax, based on Google's open-source Jax technology and running on Google Cloud, has already been used to enhance features in Apple Maps, Siri, and search tools. Although employees are prohibited from using Apple GPT for customer-facing features, it's used for product prototyping, and the company plans a significant AI announcement next year.

title: Netflix Strategic Changes Led to User Base Expansion & Record Revenues in Q2 2023
summary: Netflix's strategic changes, including a crackdown on password sharing and the introduction of an ad-supported tier, significantly boosted its user base and revenue in Q2 2023. The company added 5.89 million subscribers and achieved record revenues of $8.187 billion, demonstrating the positive impact of these initiatives despite increasing competition in the direct-to-consumer market. Even with these successes, challenges remain, such as intense competition and the absence of live sports content, which are critical for long-term growth and investor satisfaction.

The rebalance, effective July 24, will prompt funds tracking the index to adjust their portfolios, potentially leading to trading costs and minor market volatility.

title: Apple faces $1 billion UK lawsuit by apps developers over app store fees
summary: Apple is facing a 785-million-pound ($1 billion) class action lawsuit in the UK brought by over 1,500 app developers. The lawsuit alleges that Apple's App Store fees, ranging from 15% to 30% for in-app purchases, are excessive and abusive due to its monopoly on app distribution. Sean Ennis, a former OECD economist, is leading the legal action, claiming the charges harm both developers and app buyers.

title: Introducing Norton Genie - Real-Time AI-powered Scam Detection at Your Fingertips
summary: Norton has launched Norton Genie, a real-time AI-powered scam detection tool designed to help users identify and avoid increasingly sophisticated scams in texts, emails, websites, and social media posts. Available now in early access in the US, Genie combines Norton's cybersecurity expertise with advanced AI trained on millions of scam messages. The tool offers fast, free, and easy scam analysis, evolving protection, and trusted advice on how to respond to potential threats.

title: Why is Netflix lagging FAANG stocks?

The article discusses investment approaches for FAANG stocks through ETFs.

title: Apple, Meta, Google argue they're not 'bookies' in casino app appeal
summary: Apple, Meta, and Google are appealing a 2022 ruling that found them potentially liable for facilitating purchases of virtual chips in casino game apps, arguing that this interpretation of Section 230 could jeopardize the entire internet economy. They contend that holding platforms liable for payment processing related to third-party content would force extensive monitoring and is a misinterpretation of existing legal precedents. The companies emphasize they act as publishers offering payment services, not creators of the allegedly illegal apps or chips, and that their conduct in these cases is distinct from prior rulings.

The author advises widening the spread while keeping the number of contracts low to balance premium and risk, ensuring sustainable growth rather than just profitability.

The article highlights that while the market is in an uptrend, unlike the 2011 downgrade, the potential for a sharper sell-off exists, especially with upcoming economic data like the nonfarm payrolls report and earnings from tech giants set to influence market sentiment.

title: Haus raises $17M Series A led by Insight Partners to build the future of growth intelligence
summary: Haus, a growth command center utilizing causal inference, experimentation, and AI, has successfully raised $17 million in Series A funding. The round was led by Insight Partners, with participation from existing investors, to further expand its team and develop integrated causal analytical tools. This funding aims to help companies measure and drive profitable growth amid challenges like cookie depreciation and increasing consumer privacy regulations.

title: Apple sees sales slump continuing, shares drop 2% despite beating sales expectations
summary: Apple shares dropped 2% after the company forecast a continued sales slump for the current quarter, despite beating Wall Street's sales and profit targets in the fiscal third quarter. While services and China sales were strong, weaker-than-expected iPhone sales disappointed investors, raising concerns about future volume growth. Apple also revealed increased R&D spending, partly driven by generative AI development.

title: Apple Loses Historic $3 Trillion Crown as Sales Disappoint
summary: Apple Inc. saw its market capitalization fall decisively below $3 trillion after its fourth-quarter outlook raised concerns about weak demand for its products. Shares dropped 4.8% on Friday, wiping out over $160 billion in market value, marking its largest decline since September. This follows Apple becoming the first company to hit a $3 trillion valuation in June.

title: Apple Pay reportedly coming to Chile this month after long delay
summary: Apple Pay is reportedly launching in Chile in August 2023, after several previous delays and false starts since 2021. Local banks, including Santander and Banco de Chile, are expected to support the service, though some concerns remain about meeting Apple's operational and security standards. Chile would join several other Latin American countries where Apple Pay has already launched.

title: After Earnings, Is Berkshire Hathaway Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Morningstar analyzes Berkshire Hathaway's Q2 earnings, noting stronger insurance results offset by declines in BNSF and other segments. The article evaluates the stock's valuation, finding it fairly valued despite strong operating earnings and significant cash holdings, and discusses the economic moat, risks, and bull/bear cases for BRK.B.

title: Exploring two covered call strategies by Global X ETFs
summary: This article explores two covered call ETF strategies offered by Global X ETFs, designed to provide alternative income solutions in a potentially rising-rate environment. It details the Global X S&P 500 Covered Call UCITS ETF (XYLU LN) and the Global X Nasdaq 100 Covered Call UCITS ETF (QYLD LN), explaining how they generate income through option premiums and their potential benefits in volatile or sideways markets. The strategies aim to offer higher yields than traditional fixed income while potentially reducing volatility compared to underlying stocks.

title: BlackRock Inc. Boosts Stake in Moelis & Co
summary: BlackRock Inc. significantly increased its stake in independent investment bank Moelis & Co, acquiring over 1.5 million shares on July 31, 2023. This transaction now gives BlackRock a 10.40% stake in Moelis & Co. The article analyzes both firms and discusses potential implications for value investors, noting Moelis & Co's overvaluation but strong profitability and momentum.

title: LAFFER|TENGLER Equity Income ETF Review and Aggregate Rating (TGLR) $TGLR
summary: The LAFFER|TENGLER Equity Income ETF (TGLR) has an aggregate rating of "Moderate Buy" with an aggregate price target of $37.82, based on 707 analyst ratings for its 25 underlying companies, which comprise 86.9% of its portfolio. The ETF's holdings include major companies like Lam Research, Walmart, Goldman Sachs, and American Express, with various individual stock ratings from "Hold" to "Buy" and "Moderate Buy." Investors can access detailed consensus ratings and price targets for each of the top holdings.

title: Carlyle buys into Quest Global, invests $500 million
summary: Private equity firm Carlyle Group is investing $500 million to acquire a 28% stake in Quest Global Services, an engineering and R&D services provider, at a valuation of $1.8 billion. This investment will buy out existing stakeholders like Bain Capital, Advent Capital, and GIC of Singapore. Quest Global, which counts Airbus, BMW, and Rolls Royce among its clients, plans to use the funds for acquisitions and to prepare for an initial public offering within the next three to five years, with founder Ajit Prabhu also increasing his stake.

title: ¿Eres cliente de Banco de Chile? Conoce cómo añadir tus tarjetas a Apple Pay
summary: This article explains how Banco de Chile customers can add their credit and debit cards to Apple Pay, which recently launched in Chile. It details the steps for setting up cards via the Apple Wallet app or directly through the Banco de Chile's Mi Banco app, highlighting the security and convenience of using Apple Pay for transactions both domestically and internationally.

title: TechInsights Teardown: Apple iPhone 14 Plus
summary: This article details a partial teardown of the Apple iPhone 14 Plus conducted by TechInsights, outlining its key specifications and components. It examines the main board, sensor flex board, and RF board, identifying various manufacturers like Apple, Samsung, Qualcomm, and others that supply parts for the device. The article concludes with a breakdown of the major component costs within the smartphone.

title: Dropbox review: Still the best at syncing and sharing
summary: This PCWorld review reaffirms Dropbox's position as a top choice for fast, reliable file synchronization and sharing, despite its limited free storage and lack of intermediate subscription tiers. While it excels in its core functionality and offers business-oriented features, its pricing model lacks options between the free 2GB and the paid 2TB. The article highlights its strengths for collaborative file access and its backup capabilities.

title: Ford taps Apple exec to build high-margin digital services
summary: Ford Motor has appointed former Apple executive Peter Stern as president of its new Ford Integrated Services unit to develop high-margin digital and subscription services. This move aligns with Ford's strategy to generate recurring revenue from vehicle-connected services, similar to Apple's model with its hardware. Stern will focus on integrating hardware, software, and services across Ford's various units, with a particular emphasis on expanding its BlueCruise hands-free driving package.

title: What To Consider When Using Generative AI
summary: The article discusses the considerations for using generative AI tools in a business context, focusing on security risks like data leakage and accuracy issues such as hallucinations. It highlights how consumer generative AI tools can pose dangers for sensitive corporate information and accuracy, leading many companies to restrict their use. The piece concludes by advocating for enterprise-specific generative AI solutions, like C3 Generative AI, that are designed for secure and reliable data handling to mitigate these risks.

title: Production of Apple iPhone 15 reportedly kicks off in India
summary: Apple has reportedly started the production of its upcoming iPhone 15 in India through its main manufacturer, Foxconn, at a facility in Tamil Nadu. This move is part of Apple's strategy to reduce its reliance on China for manufacturing and aims to shorten the lag time between Indian and Chinese assembled iPhones. The iPhone 15 is anticipated to be unveiled in September, with other manufacturers like Pegatron also expected to begin production in India soon.

title: Apple Card named Best Co-Branded Credit Card for Customer Satisfaction with No Annual Fee by J.D. Power
summary: Apple Card, issued by Goldman Sachs, has been recognized for the third consecutive year as the Best Co-Branded Credit Card for Customer Satisfaction with No Annual Fee by J.D. Power. This award highlights Apple Card's commitment to user financial health, including features like Daily Cash rewards and the recently launched Savings account, which has accumulated over $10 billion in deposits. Apple and Goldman Sachs continue to collaborate on expanding the value and benefits offered to Apple Card users.

title: WEBTOON is ready to take on Apple and Amazon (and win)
summary: WEBTOON's CEO, Kim Junkoo, is confident his company can compete with tech giants like Apple and Amazon in the digital comic space, citing their unique creator economy and extensive user data. Despite Amazon and Apple Japan launching their own vertical scroll comic formats, Junkoo believes these companies cannot replicate WEBTOON's developed ecosystem and massive user base of 85.6 million, largely under 30, and nearly a million creators. He suggests that if big tech were serious about the IP-creating business, they would have to acquire WEBTOON.

title: Nine million and counting: The controversial shopping app sweeping Australia
summary: Temu, a Chinese-owned online marketplace, has rapidly become Australia's fastest-growing shopping app, amassing over 9.2 million users since its April launch. Despite its popularity driven by low prices and strong advertising, Temu faces controversy regarding alleged forced labor, counterfeit goods, and a lack of financial transparency from its parent company, PDD Holdings. The article highlights Temu's significant market presence and the ethical questions surrounding its operations.

title: Congress Large Cap Growth ETF Holdings
summary: The Congress Large Cap Growth ETF (CAML), established on August 22, 2023, is an actively managed fund investing in large-cap companies for long-term capital growth. With $333.49 million in assets under management and 41 holdings, its top investments include NVIDIA, Apple, and Alphabet. The ETF focuses on companies anticipated to experience earnings growth.

title: The best ETFs for retirement income
summary: This article explores the best ETFs for retirement income, focusing on conservative asset allocation ETFs and tactical overlays for retirees. It discusses how these ETFs can help reduce volatility, hedge inflation, and generate income, with insights from financial experts on their suitability for different risk tolerances and financial situations. The author also delves into defensive sector ETFs and low-volatility ETFs as additional strategies for Canadian retirees.

title: Arm, the Chip Designer, Files for an I.P.O. Expected to Be Among the Largest (Published 2023)
summary: Arm, the chip design company owned by SoftBank, has filed for an initial public offering (IPO) on the Nasdaq exchange, which is anticipated to be one of the largest in recent years. This move follows Nvidia's abandoned bid to acquire Arm for $40 billion 18 months prior. The IPO will provide SoftBank with additional capital for investments, and SoftBank will retain its position as Arm's controlling shareholder.

title: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Second Quarter Fiscal 2024
summary: NVIDIA reported record revenue of $13.51 billion for the second quarter of fiscal 2024, a 101% increase from a year ago, driven by strong growth in Data Center revenue at $10.32 billion. The company also announced a new $25.00 billion share repurchase authorization and provided a positive outlook for the third quarter, expecting revenue of $16.00 billion. The CEO highlighted the ongoing transition to accelerated computing and generative AI as key drivers for NVIDIA's success.

title: Invesco S&P 500 Revenue ETF (RWL) Stock Price, Holdings, Dividend Yield
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the Invesco S&P 500 Revenue ETF (RWL), including its current stock price, key financial metrics like PE ratio and dividend yield, and its top holdings as of November 30, 2025. It also covers the ETF's performance data, asset allocation, and recent trades. The fund holds 502 stocks with Walmart, Amazon, and Apple among its largest positions.

title: John Warnock, Inventor of the PDF, Dies at 82
summary: John Warnock, co-founder of Adobe Systems and inventor of the ubiquitous Portable Document Format (PDF), died on August 19 at the age of 82. His innovations in computer graphics, including PostScript and PDF, were instrumental in enabling modern personal computing and visually rich digital experiences. Warnock's persistent goal was to ensure consistent document rendering across different computers and printers.

title: Early Apple computer that helped launch $3T company sells at auction for $223K
summary: One of the first Apple-1 personal computers, signed by co-founder Steve Wozniak, recently sold at auction for over $223,000. This fully operational vintage computer was one of about 200 manufactured in Apple co-founder Steve Jobs' garage in the 1970s, contributing to the launch of the now multi-trillion dollar company. The auction also included the sale of an original handwritten advertisement by Jobs and an early Apple company check signed by both Jobs and Wozniak.

title: iShares Russell 1000 ETF (IWB) Stock Price, Holdings, Dividend Yield
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the iShares Russell 1000 ETF (IWB), including its current stock price, key statistics like PE and PB ratios, and dividend yield. It outlines the ETF's top holdings as of December 31, 2025, which include major tech companies like NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft, and details its asset allocation and historical performance. The report also highlights the ETF's financial strength and profitability rankings from GuruFocus.

title: 'Not just money and math': Young people are willing to sacrifice returns for ESG
summary: New data reveals that young investors are increasingly willing to sacrifice investment returns to align their portfolios with environmental, social, and governance (ESG) causes they care about. This trend is particularly strong among Gen Z and millennials, with many prepared to underperform market averages for values-aligned investments. Behavioral scientists suggest this reflects a need for young people to signal their values and identity through their investment choices.

title: Corporate America’s Chief Critic, Carl Icahn, Gets His Comeuppance (Published 2023)
summary: Carl Icahn, a notorious activist investor, recently faced a challenge from short seller Nathan Anderson, who questioned the financial stability of Icahn Enterprises, Icahn's publicly traded company. This led to Icahn Enterprises cutting its dividend by half. The situation is seen as an embarrassing turn for Icahn, as he experienced tactics similar to those he has often used against other companies.

title: Hedge fund exposure to 7 biggest tech stocks at record high, Goldman Sachs says
summary: Hedge funds have reached record exposure to the seven largest tech stocks by market capitalization, according to Goldman Sachs data, driven by strong performance and the artificial intelligence theme. These seven stocks, including Nvidia, Apple, and Microsoft, now constitute about 20% of the total net market value held by hedge funds tracked by Goldman Sachs. Despite the concentration risk, investment managers rationalize these allocations due to the significant returns generated by these companies this year.

title: Apellis to lay off 25% of staff, trim research in major restructuring
summary: Apellis Pharmaceuticals announced a major restructuring, including a 25% workforce reduction (about 225 employees) and trimmed research spending, to focus resources on its newly approved vision loss drug, Syfovre. This move is expected to save up to $300 million through 2024, helping to extend its operational runway. The restructuring follows a sudden stock price decline spurred by reports of rare but potentially blinding side effects associated with Syfovre, though the company suggests these issues might be unrelated to the drug itself.

title: Invesco Next Gen Connectivity ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:KNCT)
summary: The Invesco Next Gen Connectivity ETF (KNCT) is an exchange-traded fund launched on June 23, 2005, that invests in companies generating at least 50% of their revenue from future connectivity technologies. It tracks a passively managed index and currently has $131.66 million in assets under management. Its top holdings include Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, Apple, and Broadcom.

title: Apple partner Globalstar taps former Qualcomm executive Paul Jacobs as CEO
summary: Globalstar, the satellite firm partnering with Apple for emergency communication services, has appointed former Qualcomm CEO Paul Jacobs as its new chief executive, replacing David Kagan. The announcement led to a nearly 20% surge in Globalstar's shares. Jacobs' appointment also involves a deal between Globalstar and XCOM Labs, a wireless tech startup he co-founded, for exclusive access to certain technologies and personnel.

title: Globalstar Names XCOM Labs Founder Paul Jacobs as CEO
summary: Globalstar, an international telecom infrastructure provider, has appointed Paul Jacobs, founder and CEO of XCOM Labs and former CEO of Qualcomm, as its new CEO. Jacobs brings extensive experience and a proven track record in the wireless industry, with a focus on innovation and growth. The appointment coincides with a strategic perpetual licensing agreement with XCOM Labs, granting Globalstar exclusive access to key XCOM technologies and personnel to drive strategic initiatives and deliver innovative solutions.

title: Globalstar hires former Qualcomm CEO for 'next phase'
summary: Globalstar has appointed Paul Jacobs, former Qualcomm CEO, as its new CEO and will license technology from his XCOM Labs startup. Jacobs will lead Globalstar during a crucial period, as the company's satellites power Apple's iPhone emergency calling functions and it prepares to expand its IoT services and leverage its Band 53 spectrum. The licensing agreement with XCOM Labs, valued at approximately $64 million in stock, grants Globalstar exclusive access to XCOM's capacity-multiplying technology for its Band 53 spectrum.

title: How space traffic in orbit could spell trouble on Earth
summary: The increasing number of satellites in Earth's orbit, particularly large constellations like Starlink, significantly raises the risk of catastrophic collisions and the generation of more space debris. Such collisions could disrupt vital services on Earth, including GPS, communication, weather forecasting, and intelligence gathering. The current patchwork of international regulations is insufficient to manage this growing traffic, highlighting the urgent need for a formal, coordinated global system to prevent disasters and maintain the functionality of orbital infrastructure.

title: Apple announces next Impact Accelerator class for businesses advancing environmental innovation
summary: Apple has announced its third Impact Accelerator class, a cohort of 12 Black-, Hispanic/Latinx-, and Indigenous-owned businesses focused on environmental solutions and green technology. This program is part of Apple's Racial Equity and Justice Initiative, aiming to help diverse businesses scale their impact and contribute to a greener, more equitable future. The participating companies offer solutions addressing climate change, resource management, and smarter chemistry, and will receive extensive support and mentorship from Apple.

title: The Fishbowl: Lydia Parker, Samsung Ads Europe
summary: This article features an interview with Lydia Parker, Head of International Agencies at Samsung Ads Europe, as part of The Media Leader's "Fishbowl" series. She discusses her career progression, professional experiences, leadership strategies in a hybrid work environment, changes in client conversations due to the booming CTV market, and her favorite ad.

title: Details on InvestigateTV+
summary: InvestigateTV+ launched its new weekday news magazine program on September 11, featuring groundbreaking investigations from Gray’s award-winning team, national reporters, and stories on consumer issues, health, and inspiration. Full episodes are available on their website and dedicated apps (Roku, Amazon Fire, AppleTV), alongside their weekend show focusing on longform investigative journalism. The article also lists recent topics covered by InvestigateTV+.

title: Globalstar taps SpaceX to launch Apple's Emergency SOS satellites
summary: Globalstar has partnered with SpaceX to launch satellites for Apple's Emergency SOS iPhone feature by 2025, with Apple funding 95% of the costs, including the $64 million launch fee. This agreement is notable given an ongoing regulatory dispute where Globalstar accuses SpaceX of attempting to secure radio spectrum vital for its own satellite services. The Emergency SOS feature, exclusively reliant on Globalstar's network for iPhone 14 and newer models, allows users to connect to satellites for emergency help without cellular or Wi-Fi.

title: IXN: Not A True Global Tech Play
summary: The iShares Global Tech ETF (IXN) is criticized for its misleading name, as it is heavily concentrated in U.S.-based tech giants like Apple, Microsoft, and Nvidia, comprising nearly two-thirds of its portfolio. Despite its "global" designation, over 80% of its holdings are U.S. companies, limiting true international exposure and sector diversification. This article highlights that IXN is not a genuinely global technology investment, potentially making investors vulnerable if they seek diversified international tech exposure.

title: SAP nabs new global AI head from Microsoft, Walter Sun
summary: SAP has appointed Walter Sun, formerly VP of Copilot Applied Artificial Intelligence at Microsoft, as its new global head of AI. This strategic hire underscores SAP's commitment to prioritizing AI, following recent collaborations with Microsoft and Google Cloud to integrate generative AI into its enterprise offerings. Sun, with his extensive background in AI and machine learning, is tasked with leveraging SAP's broad applications and customer base to transform business operations through innovative AI solutions.

title: An Apple-leased building in Sunnyvale sold for $41M
summary: A Miami real estate firm, BentallGreenOak, purchased an Apple-leased office-and-research building in Sunnyvale for $41 million. This transaction highlights ongoing commercial real estate activity in Silicon Valley. The article briefly mentions the high price paid for the property.

title: Claim Construction – We Agree . . . Or Do We? – One-E-Way, Inc. v. Apple Inc.
summary: This article discusses the Federal Circuit's decision in *One-E-Way v. Apple*, highlighting a dispute over a previously agreed-upon claim construction for "unique user code." The case illustrates that even agreed-upon claim constructions can lead to significant disagreements regarding their application to accused products, with Apple successfully arguing that the code must be associated with a user, not just a device. The ruling serves as a cautionary tale for litigants to ensure proposed claim constructions provide absolute clarity and are well-supported by intrinsic evidence.

title: Qualcomm CEO says AI may breathe new life into smartphones: 'It could create a new upgrade cycle'
summary: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon believes artificial intelligence could spark a new upgrade cycle for smartphones, revitalizing a market that saw a significant sales decline in 2022. Amon indicated that the company's upcoming Snapdragon Summit in October would showcase new AI-driven use cases from smartphone manufacturers. Unlike Nvidia's focus on data centers, Qualcomm aims to bring AI capabilities directly to devices, enhancing user experience and driving demand for new models.

title: India's policy contradictions are making it harder for investors to crack its market
summary: India's apparent policy contradictions, such as import restrictions on electronics despite efforts to attract foreign investment, are complicating the market for global investors. While Prime Minister Modi's "Make in India" initiative and production-linked incentives aim to boost domestic manufacturing and attract companies like Apple and Foxconn, protectionist measures and capital controls create uncertainty. These challenges exist even as India seeks to enhance its global reputation and capitalize on shifting geopolitical alliances and supply chain diversification away from China, potentially limiting its full economic growth and investment appeal.

title: Nvidia Says It Will Invest In Arm’s IPO After Failed Acquisition
summary: Nvidia has confirmed its intention to invest in Arm's initial public offering, despite its failed acquisition attempt of the company. The GPU giant was named as a potential "cornerstone investor" in Arm's updated IPO filing, alongside other tech companies like Intel, AMD, Apple, and Google. This investment highlights the continued importance of Arm's architecture to Nvidia's products and the broader tech ecosystem.

title: Why Goldman Sachs believes that Spotify will remain the world’s dominant music streaming service in 2030
summary: Goldman Sachs predicts that Spotify will remain the dominant music streaming service globally through 2030, maintaining its market share around the mid-30% level outside of China. Despite facing competition from larger tech conglomerates and new services like TikTok Music, Spotify's market share outside of China has remained broadly stable since 2017. Goldman Sachs also anticipates YouTube Music will become the second-largest DSP by 2030, surpassing Apple Music, and foresees consolidation among smaller streaming platforms.

title: Everything Apple Plans to Show on Sept. 12: iPhone 15, Watches, AirPods
summary: Apple Inc. is set to unveil its latest products on September 12, including the iPhone 15 line, new smartwatches, and the latest AirPods. The event is expected to highlight the titanium iPhone 15 Pro, camera improvements, a switch to USB-C chargers, and faster smartwatches. This launch represents Apple's most significant new product unveiling of the year.

title: If You Like SPHQ, Check Out Quality ETFs XMHQ and XSHQ
summary: The article highlights the growing popularity of quality ETFs, specifically discussing the Invesco S&P 500 Quality ETF (SPHQ) and suggesting that investors also consider mid-cap and small-cap quality ETFs like XMHQ and XSHQ for broader exposure. It emphasizes that quality factors are significant across all market capitalizations and details how these Invesco funds select their holdings based on quality scores. The piece also provides insights into the AUM and recent inflows for each ETF, noting the key differences and similarities in how they track quality within their respective market segments.

title: Self-care products set to grow big; no downtrading in healthcare, says Haleon CEO
summary: Haleon CEO Brian McNamara states that the self-care products market is poised for significant growth, driven by an increased focus on preventive healthcare post-pandemic and consumers' unwillingness to compromise on health. He notes that governments worldwide are also promoting self-care to alleviate pressure on healthcare systems. India is identified as a crucial growth market for Haleon, where the company sees little "downtrading" in healthcare products, including brands like Sensodyne.

title: History of Apple in Photos, From Steve Jobs Era to $3 Trillion
summary: This article chronicles the history of Apple, from its founding by Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak to its recent achievement of a $3 trillion market cap under Tim Cook. It details key product launches like the Apple II, Macintosh, iPod, and iPhone, as well as leadership changes and challenges such as the recent DOJ lawsuit and declining iPhone sales in China. The article also touches upon Apple's expansion into services and new product categories like the Apple Watch and Vision Pro, alongside its pivot towards generative AI.

title: The pros and cons of the Vanguard FTSE All-World ex-US ETF (VEU)
summary: The Vanguard FTSE All-World ex-US ETF (VEU) offers extensive geographic and business diversification with over 3,700 holdings and a low annual management fee of 0.08%. While it provides exposure to many strong global companies outside the US, its exclusion of US businesses means it misses out on some top performers like Apple and Microsoft, which have driven higher returns in US-inclusive international ETFs. Despite this, VEU remains a strong choice for investors seeking broad non-US market exposure.

title: Qualcomm will make Apple’s iPhone modems until 2026, and its stock surges
summary: Qualcomm Inc. will continue to supply modem chips for Apple Inc.’s iPhones until at least 2026. This extended partnership suggests Apple's efforts to develop its own 5G modem chips are progressing slower than anticipated. Following the announcement, Qualcomm's stock (QCOM) experienced a significant surge of approximately 4%.

title: Qualcomm, Meta Platforms rise; J.M. Smucker, RTX fall, Monday, 9/11/2023
summary: This article details the stock performance of several companies on Monday, September 11, 2023. Qualcomm and Meta Platforms saw their stock prices rise due to specific company news, while J.M. Smucker and RTX experienced declines following significant announcements. Other notable movers include Alibaba, FuelCell Energy, Carlisle Cos., and Freeport-McMoRan.

title: Qualcomm to supply Apple Inc with 5G chips until 2026 under new deal
summary: Qualcomm has signed a new deal with Apple to supply 5G chips for iPhones until at least 2026, extending their previous agreement which was set to expire this year. While the financial terms are similar to the prior deal, Qualcomm's financial projections assume that only 20% of iPhones will use its chips by 2026, as Apple continues to develop its own modem technology. A patent licensing deal between the companies, signed in 2019, remains in place and could be extended beyond its 2025 expiration.

title: Paul Jacobs Tapped to Lead Globalstar
summary: Former Qualcomm Technologies CEO Paul Jacobs has been named the new CEO of Globalstar, coinciding with a licensing agreement that gives Globalstar exclusive access to certain XCOM Labs technologies and personnel. This deal, valued at approximately $63.6 million, aims to leverage Globalstar's terrestrial spectrum with XCOM's high-performance wireless technology. The move is expected to drive innovation in satellite communications and enhance value for Globalstar shareholders.

title: The hottest back-to-school accessory? A location sharing app
summary: Location sharing apps are becoming increasingly popular among American families, with Life360 reporting a significant surge in sign-ups this year. While many parents use these apps to track their children for safety, especially as kids gain independence, experts debate whether this constant surveillance truly reduces anxiety or hinders a child's development of self-reliance. Life360's founder, Chris Hulls, was inspired to create the app after Hurricane Katrina highlighted the need for family tracking technology, aiming to provide peace of mind for loved ones.

title: Apple introduces the advanced new Apple Watch Series 9
summary: Apple introduced the Apple Watch Series 9, featuring the new S9 SiP chip, a brighter display, faster on-device Siri, and a magical new double tap gesture. This release marks Apple's first carbon-neutral products, aligning with its Apple 2030 goal to be carbon neutral across its entire business, manufacturing, and product life cycle by 2030. The new watch also runs watchOS 10 and introduces FineWoven bands as a leather alternative, along with new Nike and Hermès band collections.

title: Apple unveils iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max
summary: Apple has unveiled the iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max, featuring a strong and lightweight titanium design, a new customizable Action button, significant camera upgrades, and the A17 Pro chip for enhanced performance and gaming. The new models also support USB-C with faster speeds and introduce new safety features like Roadside Assistance via satellite. Pre-orders begin September 15, with availability starting September 22.

title: Apple unveils its first carbon neutral products
summary: Apple announced its first carbon neutral products, primarily the new Apple Watch lineup, marking significant progress towards its Apple 2030 goal of making every product carbon neutral. The company detailed innovations in design, clean energy use in manufacturing and product use, reduced transportation emissions, and the development of new materials like FineWoven which replaces leather. Apple also introduced a new tool called Grid Forecast to help users choose cleaner energy times for electricity consumption.

title: All else being equal: Making the case for equal-weight ETFs
summary: This article discusses the advantages and disadvantages of equal-weight ETFs compared to market-cap-weighted ETFs, particularly in the context of the S&P 500's concentration in a few large tech companies. It highlights how equal weighting can manage concentration and valuation risk, offer a value investment style tilt, and increase exposure to smaller, well-established companies. While equal-weight strategies may underperform when market gains are driven by a select few, they can offer diversification benefits and a "buy-low, sell-high" approach through rebalancing.

title: Apple Inc. stock outperforms competitors despite losses on the day
summary: Shares of Apple Inc. (AAPL) fell by 1.71% to $176.30 on Tuesday, despite outperforming competitors on a day that saw general market losses with the NASDAQ Composite Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average also declining. This drop ended Apple's two-day winning streak.

title: Apple unveils iPhone 15 Pro with titanium case, holds line on prices
summary: Apple announced a new series of iPhones, including the iPhone 15 Pro with a titanium shell and improved features, while maintaining prices despite a global smartphone slump. The launch comes amidst economic uncertainty and increased competition in crucial markets like China. Apple also highlighted new watches and its commitment to becoming carbon neutral.

title: Apple unveils its first carbon neutral products
summary: Apple has announced its first carbon neutral products, including models of the new Apple Watch lineup, as a significant step towards its Apple 2030 goal to make every product carbon neutral. This achievement results from innovations in design, substantial reductions in emissions, and advancements in clean energy use throughout its supply chain. The company has also eliminated leather from its product lines, introduced fiber-based packaging, and launched Grid Forecast in the Home app to help users optimize electricity consumption with cleaner energy sources.

title: Trading the Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) in Different Markets
summary: Historically, the TLT ETF had lower options premiums due to its low implied volatility compared to SPY. However, post-2020 economic changes, including the Fed's interest rate hikes, significantly increased TLT's implied volatility, making selling premium potentially more profitable. Research suggests that while lower-IV environments didn't yield substantial profits, higher-IV periods, especially with management at 21 DTE, show enhanced performance for selling premium in TLT.

title: Arm, the Chip Designer, Raises $4.87 Billion in the Year’s Largest I.P.O. (Published 2023)
summary: Arm, the British chip design company, successfully raised $4.87 billion in the largest initial public offering of the year, valuing the company at $54.5 billion. This I.P.O. is a significant event for SoftBank, which acquired Arm in 2016 and aims to capitalize on the tech industry's focus on artificial intelligence, following a failed acquisition bid by Nvidia. Arm's return to public markets under the ticker symbol ARM is being closely watched as a gauge of investor interest in new tech offerings.

title: Netgear's Nighthawk MK93S Mesh Router Arrives As iPhone 15 Readies A Big Wi-Fi 6E Push
summary: Netgear has launched its Nighthawk MK93S, a tri-band Wi-Fi 6E mesh router system, timed with the release of the iPhone 15 series. This system offers speeds up to 50% faster than its predecessor and covers homes up to 7,500 square feet. Netgear anticipates that the iPhone 15's adoption of Wi-Fi 6E will significantly boost the technology's market presence and consumer adoption.

title: Chipmaker Arm is valued at $55 billion after a blockbuster IPO that is this year's biggest by far
summary: Arm Holdings successfully priced its IPO at the top of its range, raising $4.87 billion and achieving a valuation of approximately $54.5 billion. This marks the largest listing of the year globally and is expected to invigorate the equity markets and a pipeline of other tech IPOs. SoftBank will retain about 90% ownership after the offering, which saw significant investment from major tech companies like Intel, Apple, and Nvidia.

title: Arm climbs 25% in Nasdaq debut after pricing IPO at $51 a share
summary: Arm Holdings saw its stock jump nearly 25% on its first day of trading on the Nasdaq after pricing its IPO at $51 per share, valuing the company at almost $60 billion. summary: Jabil, a St. Petersburg-based tech company, is partnering with California-based Calix Inc. to manufacture parts for expanding broadband internet service in rural America. summary: Qualcomm has successfully defeated a consumer antitrust lawsuit in California federal court, which alleged that the chipmaker's contracts with device manufacturers artificially inflated mobile phone costs. U.S. District Judge Jacqueline Scott Corley ruled in favor of Qualcomm, stating that allowing the plaintiffs to revive past evidence would lead to prolonged and expensive "do-over litigation." summary: Apple has been ordered to face a private antitrust lawsuit brought by payment card issuers. The lawsuit alleges that Apple exerts a 100% monopoly over the domestic market for tap-and-pay wallets on its devices, forcing banks to pay excessive fees and hindering competition and innovation. summary: French competition authorities raided Nvidia's offices on suspicion of anticompetitive practices related to cloud computing and graphics cards. summary: The Dutch competition watchdog ACM has rejected Apple's objections to 50 million euros ($53 million) in fines. The fines were imposed because Apple failed to fully comply with orders to allow alternative payment methods for dating apps in the Netherlands. Apple plans to appeal the decision to the Netherlands courts, maintaining that the original order degrades investment incentives and compromises user privacy and data security.

summary: A new paper from Moody's Analytics identifies the "cheesecake factor," suggesting that the presence of a Cheesecake Factory restaurant indicates a mall's financial health. summary: PayPal has fulfilled its promise to integrate its PayPal and Venmo credit and debit cards with Apple Wallet, nearly a year after the initial vow. This integration allows users to add their cards to Apple Pay for in-app and Safari browser transactions. Former CEO Dan Schulman stated that this move aims to offer more choice to PayPal's merchants and increase branded transactions, citing a similar success with Google Pay in Germany.

summary: BlackBerry announced its intention to split into two distinct businesses: IoT and cybersecurity. Morningstar analysts view this separation positively, especially the IoT business which includes the QNX software for autonomous vehicles, as it is considered the most valuable part of the firm and an attractive investment. The cybersecurity segment, while struggling, is also expected to benefit from better execution as a separate entity and could be an attractive buyout candidate.

summary: Treasury yields surged to their highest levels in over a decade as traders anticipated prolonged high borrowing costs from the Federal Reserve, impacting most US stocks. summary: Sundar Pichai, years before becoming Google’s CEO, expressed concerns in 2007 emails to co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin regarding the "bad optics" of Google's exclusive search deal with Apple. These emails, used as evidence in a Justice Department antitrust case, revealed Pichai's discomfort with Google being the sole search provider in the Safari browser. The company is trying to diversify into new markets like IoT, VR, and automotive chips, but its revenue continues to be heavily reliant on the struggling smartphone market.

This fake app, distributed via a lookalike website, aimed to steal sensitive user data like contacts, call logs, and SMS messages, exploiting the critical need for rocket alert systems. Users who sideloaded the Android version from the malicious site are advised to delete the app and reinstall the legitimate version from the Play Store.

Qualcomm currently holds an exclusivity agreement with Microsoft for Arm-based Windows chips, which is set to expire by the end of the year, potentially opening the door for Nvidia and AMD.

summary: KT announced a collaboration with Thailand’s Jasmine Group to develop a Thai Large Language Model (LLM) using KT's "Mi:dm" super-scale AI, marking the first overseas venture for a domestically produced super-scale AI. The partnership involves sharing technical expertise for LLM development, establishing a GPU farm, and exploring global LLM business models in Southeast Asia. Both companies aim to enhance Thailand's AI industry competitiveness and expand into other regional markets.

summary: Nvidia is developing Arm-based processors for personal computers, aiming to compete with Intel and Qualcomm, with availability expected as soon as 2025. This move intensifies competition in the PC chip market, especially as AMD is also reportedly working on Arm-based processors for PCs. The initiative follows Apple's successful transition to in-house Arm-based chips, boosting Mac sales, and poses a significant challenge to Intel's dominant position.

title: FDA Clears Omnipod 5 App for iPhones
summary: The FDA has granted 510(k) Clearance to the Omnipod 5 app for iPhone, making Insulet Corporation the first to offer a tubeless AID system with full control from compatible Android and iOS smartphones. This clearance follows the Omnipod 5 Automated Insulin Delivery system's initial FDA clearance for patients aged 6 years and older with type 1 diabetes in January 2022, and subsequent approval for children aged 2 years and older. The iOS app will offer the same functionality as the Android version, plus a new custom food feature, with a full market release expected in 2024.

summary: Global investors are offloading Chinese shares at an "unprecedented" rate due to concerns over China's economic slowdown, a lack of convincing policy responses, and an opaque business environment. Experts suggest that a fundamental rethinking of China investment is underway, driven by a collapse of trust in the Chinese Communist Party and rising US-China tensions.

summary: Apple announced its new M3, M3 Pro, and M3 Max chips, touting them as the most advanced chips for a personal computer. Built on 3-nanometer process technology, these chips introduce a next-generation GPU architecture with features like Dynamic Caching, hardware-accelerated ray tracing, and mesh shading, delivering significant performance improvements over the M1 family of chips. The M3 family also boasts faster CPU performance, an enhanced Neural Engine for AI/ML tasks, and an unrivaled unified memory architecture supporting up to 128GB, along with improved power efficiency for longer battery life and a reduced environmental impact.

title: BlackBerry CEO Chen to retire, director Lynch to hold interim charge
summary: BlackBerry CEO John Chen is set to retire at the end of the week after a decade of leading the company through a strategic pivot from hardware to enterprise software. Chen oversaw BlackBerry's shift to cybersecurity, in-car software, and IoT applications, and initiated plans to separate its IoT and cybersecurity units.

summary: The Walt Disney Co. is moving forward with its acquisition of Comcast Corp.’s 33% stake in the streaming service Hulu. summary: Globalstar's new CEO, Paul Jacobs, addressed the company's future plans for the first time since taking the helm approximately two months ago. summary: Chatbots are increasingly vital in virtual healthcare delivery, offering applications from administrative tasks like scheduling appointments to clinical uses such as patient triage and mental health support. While they provide significant benefits in efficiency and patient satisfaction, concerns persist regarding their ability to handle complex diagnostic scenarios, data privacy, and HIPAA compliance, requiring ongoing efforts to build trust among both physicians and patients. summary: Infosys' step-down subsidiary, Infosys McCamish Systems, experienced a cyberattack that caused the non-availability of certain applications and systems. The company is collaborating with a cybersecurity products provider and has launched an independent investigation to determine the impact on systems and data. This incident adds to a growing concern about cybersecurity, following other significant breaches and warnings of state-sponsored attacks earlier this year.

summary: Global chipmakers like Samsung Electronics, Qualcomm, Intel, and AMD are intensifying their focus on on-device AI chips for smartphones, laptops, and PCs, recognizing its potential for customized services, lower costs, and enhanced privacy compared to generative AI. This shift is expected to drive significant growth in AI-enabled consumer electronics and contribute to rising memory chip prices. Both on-device AI and generative AI are seen as complementary, with companies like Samsung planning to integrate both into future smart devices.

summary: Starbucks announced it will raise wages for its U.S. retail hourly partners by at least 3% starting January 1, 2024, with more tenured employees receiving higher increases up to 5%. This move is part of an expanded benefits package and comes without anticipated menu price increases. The company stated these investments aim to improve the partner experience, reduce turnover, and enhance customer connection scores.

summary: Warren Buffett is recognized not only for his success as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway and his strategic investments in companies like Apple and Occidental Petroleum, but also for his exceptional candor with investors. The partnership has been fruitful, contributing five recent shows to Lionsgate’s TV series slate, including "Mythic Quest" and "The Serpent Queen."

title: Apple agrees to $25 million settlement with US over hiring of immigrants
summary: Apple Inc. has agreed to pay $25 million to settle claims by the U.S. Department of Justice that it illegally favored immigrant workers over U.S. citizens and green card holders for certain jobs. The Justice Department stated that Apple did not recruit U.S. citizens or permanent residents for jobs eligible for a federal program allowing employers to sponsor immigrant workers for green cards. This settlement marks the largest ever for the Justice Department concerning discrimination based on citizenship.

title: Booking.com settles Italian tax dispute with 94-million euro payment
summary: Travel website Booking.com has agreed to pay approximately 94 million euros ($100.25 million) to settle a tax dispute in Italy covering the period from 2013 to 2021. The settlement follows an investigation by Genoa prosecutors into the company's handling of VAT on properties rented through its platform. As part of the agreement, Booking.com also filed its VAT return in Italy for 2022 and committed to acting as a tax substitute for transactions with private individuals not registered for VAT.

title: Qualcomm and Iridium end their satellite chip partnership
summary: Mobile chip giant Qualcomm has terminated its satellite-to-phone partnership with Iridium, less than a year after its announcement. The collaboration, which aimed to provide satellite-to-phone services via Snapdragon Satellite and Iridium's satellites, struggled due to a lack of adoption by smartphone manufacturers who preferred standards-based solutions. Both companies plan to continue exploring standards-based satellite connectivity options, with Iridium now free to engage directly with OEMs and chipmakers.

title: Amazon sued over 'dangerous partnership' with virtual casino apps
summary: Amazon is being sued in a proposed consumer class-action lawsuit for allegedly earning billions through an "illegal internet gambling enterprise." The lawsuit, filed by a Nevada resident, claims Amazon distributed over 30 illegal casino apps and processed payments for virtual chips, maintaining a 30% financial interest. This case is part of broader litigation targeting online social casino apps, with similar lawsuits pending against Apple, Meta, and Google regarding their payment-processing roles.

summary: This article highlights the Global X S&P 500 Covered Call ETF (XYLD) as a strategy for investors looking to reduce volatility and generate income in the current market environment. summary: The "FAANG" stock group has evolved into the "Magnificent Seven," with Netflix replaced by Nvidia, and Microsoft and Tesla added to the mix of top U.S. market names. summary: Hedgeye argues that a recession is currently underway, contrary to investor hopes for a "Santa Claus rally" and standard seasonal trends. title: Spotlight on illegal hiring practices: Apple pays $25M for recruiting, job ad mistakes
summary: Apple Inc. has agreed to pay $25 million to settle allegations of illegal hiring practices related to its PERM program. A DOJ investigation found Apple failed to recruit U.S. citizens or green card holders, did not advertise these positions on its external website, and required paper applications for PERM jobs while allowing electronic applications for others. The settlement includes $18.25 million for discrimination victims and $6.75 million for civil penalties, with Apple also agreeing to revise its recruitment practices and provide employee training.

title: FMR LLC Bolsters Portfolio with Fidelity International Value Fac
summary: FMR LLC, also known as Fidelity, has significantly expanded its investment portfolio by acquiring 350,126 shares of the Fidelity International Value Factor ETF (FIVA) at $21.95 per share. summary: FMR LLC, through its flagship company Fidelity Investments, has acquired a new stake in Magenta Therapeutics Inc (MGTA) by purchasing 2,218,212 shares at $0.6996 per share. summary: David Tepper’s Appaloosa hedge fund significantly increased its stake in Amazon.com Inc. and completely divested its position in Apple Inc. during the last quarter. title: What's next for satellite communications on Android?
summary: Apple has extended its Emergency SOS via satellite service for iPhone 14 and 15 users to two years, while Qualcomm's Snapdragon Satellite initiative for Android has failed due to lack of OEM integration. This leaves Iridium, a key satellite provider, free to pursue new partnerships directly with smartphone makers. summary: Warren Buffett has consistently invested in Berkshire Hathaway's own stock for 21 consecutive quarters, authorizing over $72 billion in repurchases since mid-2018. summary: AT&T announced its Black Friday deals for the holiday season, offering significant savings on various Apple products including the iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15, iPhone 14, iPhone 14 Pro, iPhone SE 3rd Gen, iPad, and Apple Watch. Deals include trade-in options, no trade-in required offers, and low monthly payments, catering to both new and existing customers. Additionally, AT&T highlighted benefits like flexible shopping, unlimited plans with 5G access, AT&T Fiber deals, and special discounts for military, veterans, teachers, nurses, and physicians.

summary: Brian Stelter's book "Network of Lies" examines Fox News's role in spreading election conspiracies following the 2020 election, leading to significant legal and financial repercussions, such as the Dominion settlement. summary: Sonos Inc. is planning a significant expansion into new product categories, including headphones priced over $400 and a TV set-top box. summary: Dr. Alain Mourad, Head of InterDigital’s Wireless Lab Europe, has been elected Chair of the newly formed ETSI Industry Specification Group (ISG) on Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC). summary: The U.S. Department of Justice announced a $25 million agreement with Apple Inc. to resolve allegations of discriminatory hiring practices related to the permanent labor certification (PERM) program. The settlement includes $6.75 million in civil penalties and $18.25 million for a backpay fund for victims, and mandates Apple to align PERM recruitment with its standard practices.

This dramatic reversal comes after widespread calls for Altman's reinstatement and highlights the significant influence of investors and employees on the future of the AI startup.

title: Deere must face US farmers' 'right-to-repair' lawsuits, judge rules
summary: A U.S. judge has ruled that Deere & Co must face consolidated lawsuits from farmers accusing the agricultural machinery maker of unlawfully conspiring to restrict maintenance and repair services. The judge rejected Deere's arguments for dismissal, stating that the plaintiffs met the legal thresholds to pursue their antitrust claims. This case is part of a broader "right-to-repair" movement challenging restrictive repair practices across various industries.

title: Apple announces expanded partnership with Amkor for advanced silicon packaging in the U.S.

This facility will package Apple silicon produced at the nearby TSMC fab, strengthening Apple's commitment to American manufacturing. summary: Amkor Technology Inc. plans to build a $2 billion advanced semiconductor packaging and testing facility in Peoria, Arizona, creating approximately 2,000 jobs.
